question: Your team's developer productivity agent includes a CI job that runs Claude Code with the -p flag to review merge requests for a legacy billing service. The job posts its findings as inline comments. Each time an engineer pushes a new commit, the job re-runs and posts comments again for issues that earlier runs already flagged. Which change best stops these duplicate comments?

options.text: Move the re-runs to the Message Batches API so that all findings for each commit are posted together in a single batch.
options.reason: The Message Batches API gives cost savings with a processing window of up to 24 hours, but it does not tell Claude which issues it already reported.

options.text: Pass the findings from the previous review run into the context and instruct Claude to report only issues that are new or still unaddressed.
options.reason: The guide says to include prior review findings in context on re-runs and to ask for only new or still-unaddressed issues, so that duplicate comments are avoided.

options.text: Add few-shot examples of well-written inline review comments to the review prompt so that the comments become more consistent.
options.reason: Few-shot examples improve format and consistency, but the guide's fix for duplicates is to give Claude the prior findings, which this change does not do.

options.text: Run each re-review inside the same Claude session that generated the code changes so that Claude remembers its earlier work.
options.reason: The guide says that the session that generated code is less effective at reviewing its own changes than an independent review instance, and this change gives no list of already-posted findings.
